messages.subject: Multi-state model with DA
parts:
Hello all, 
Thank you for your time :)
I am fitting a JollySaber model via multi-state and Data augmentation. 
The model has 4 hidden states. "not yet enter", "young", "Adult", "Dead".
and 3 observed states: "not seen", "Seen as young", "seen as an adult". 

I am trying to model the survival probability as a function of age and other covariates. vial the logit function, for example: 
logit(surv)=A_0 + A_1*weight + A_2*Age

The model gives correct estimates for population sizes, but the coefficient of the transition probability between the states Adult and Dead are not consistent. I tried different approaches to treat the non-observed covariates as using a 0, NA (similar modeling as Royle 2009) and using sampled values from my seen covariates. All of them without much luck. Also, I tried different scenarios in my simulated population. All of them without much luck.
Is there something that I may be missing in the modeling of the transition probability?
does anyone have any idea on how to improve the coefficients of the regression model when using DA?

Thank you for your time and comments!


Royle, J. A. (2009). Analysis of capture–recapture models with individual covariates using data augmentation. Biometrics, 65(1), 267-274.

messages.subject: Re: Multi-state model with DA
parts:
Hello, 
yes. Sorry for my vague question. 
I am trying to use a JS model as a Multi-state model (Chapter 10.3.2 from Kery, 2011)
Using the book as a template I can build the following states:

4 hidden states. "not yet enter", "young", "Adult", "Dead".
and 3 observed states: "not seen", "Seen as young", "seen as an adult".

The model can be drawn in the following way:



From here, I am able to build the transition matrix for the hidden part and the observation process. 

The entry probabilities follow a Dirichlet distribution, to ensure that they will sum up to 1. 
The transition probability from Y to A, depends on an individual covariate F
While the transition prob from A to D depends on F and the Age

The simulation that I use just considers the age and the individual covariate F to affect survival. 
I am trying to see if the model can capture this effect, by studying the parameters \alpha_1 and \alpha_2.

So far I have not found any luck. I study 4 different simulated populations:
  1. \alpha_1 and \alpha_2 different from 0
  2. \alpha_2 = 0
  3. \alpha_1 =0
  4. \alpha_1 =0 and \alpha_2 =0
In all the scenarios convergence of the model is obtained. the posterior distributions for the population size and observation probability seem to be constant. 
The posterior distribution of \alpha_1 is close to zero (and has 0 in the 95%CI), even when there is no effect (Scenario 3)
The posterior distribution of \alpha_2 has an effect on age, even where it should be zero (Scenario 2)

One final comment: 
The model works with Data Augmentation. The augmented data of my observation process and the hidden process are 1 (not seen) for the observed process. 
For the individual covariates and age, the augmented values are sampled from seen observations. 

I would like to know if there may be a fault with my idea, or just the model is not made to find such effect. 

Thank you for your help and time reading :)

--

Kéry, M., & Schaub, M. (2011). Bayesian population analysis using WinBUGS: a hierarchical perspective. Academic Press.
